hits.text: Our operational improvements during the year, while handling 5% higher volumes, helped drive improvements to income from railway operations, diluted earnings per share, and railway operating ratio (a measure of the amount of operating revenues consumed by operating expenses). For the full year, we achieved an operating ratio of 66.4%, and an adjusted operating ratio of 65.8% (see our non-GAAP reconciliations beginning on page K26), both of which improved on a year-over-year basis. We remain committed to being a safe, productive, resilient, and efficient railroad with industry-competitive margins.

hits.text: Income from railway operations, net income and diluted earnings per share increased in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily as a result of lower railway operating expenses. The reduction in our operating expenses includes lower net expenses related to the Eastern Ohio Incident and $433 million of gains on the sale of railway lines. Railway operating revenues were slightly lower as decreased fuel surcharge revenue, an adverse mix of traffic, and decreased pricing were nearly offset by increased volumes. Our railway operating ratio improved to 66.4 percent.

message.content: Let me run the calculations in smaller pieces.

**Operating efficiency and profitability, Norfolk Southern (CIK 702165), FY2022–FY2024**

Period used: fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2022, 2023 and 2024, taken from the latest annual report in the database (FY2024 Form 10-K, accession 0000702165-25-000008). All figures are consolidated, undimensioned, full-year USD.

**Disclosed values (USD, from 10-K 0000702165-25-000008)**

| Metric | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | Fact IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Railway operating revenues | 12,745M | 12,156M | 12,123M | 859715 / 859727 / 859736 |
| Income from railway operations (operating income) | 4,809M | 2,851M | 4,071M | 855238 / 855250 / 855259 |
| Pretax income | 4,130M | 2,320M | 3,329M | 850733 / 850745 / 850754 |
| Net income | 3,270M | 1,827M | 2,622M | 854451 / 854469 / 854482 |
| Railway operating ratio (disclosed) | 62.3% | 76.5% | 66.4% | report text, chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:9989 |

**Derived ratios (calculations, not disclosed fields)**
- Operating margin (operating income ÷ revenue): 37.7% (2022) → 23.5% (2023) → 33.6% (2024).
- Net margin (net income ÷ revenue): 25.7% (2022) → 15.0% (2023) → 21.6% (2024).
- Operating ratio (expenses ÷ revenue, the inverse efficiency measure): 62.3% → 76.5% → 66.4%, matching the disclosed railway operating ratio.

**What changed**
- **2022 → 2023: sharp deterioration.** Revenue fell ~4.6% while operating income dropped ~41% (4,809M → 2,851M); operating margin fell ~14.3 percentage points and net margin ~10.6 points. The operating ratio worsened by 14.2 points. The FY2024 10-K attributes the 2023 expense pressure largely to the Eastern Ohio incident, with $1,116M of incident expense recognized in 2023 versus $325M in 2024 and nil in 2022 (chunk 702165/nsc-20241231:154530).
- **2023 → 2024: substantial recovery.** Revenue was roughly flat (−0.3%), but operating income rose ~43% (2,851M → 4,071M) and net income ~44% (1,827M → 2,622M). Operating margin recovered ~10.1 percentage points and net margin ~6.6 points; the operating ratio improved 10.1 points to 66.4%. Management cites lower railway operating expenses, including lower net Eastern Ohio incident expense and $433M of gains on railway line sales, plus operational improvements while handling 5% higher volumes (chunks 702165/nsc-20241231:83338 and :84561). Adjusted operating ratio was 65.8% in 2024.
- **Two-year view:** FY2024 efficiency and profitability remain below FY2022 levels — operating margin 33.6% vs 37.7%, net margin 21.6% vs 25.7%, operating ratio 66.4% vs 62.3% — so the 2024 rebound was partial.

**Limitations**
- The question did not specify a period; I used the three most recent fiscal years available in the annual report. Quarterly data exist but were not used, to avoid mixing period lengths.
- The 2024 improvement is partly non-recurring (incident-cost normalization and $433M of line-sale gains), so the underlying operating improvement is smaller than the headline margin recovery; the company's own adjusted operating ratio (65.8%) is the cleaner comparison but is a non-GAAP measure.
- Margin and operating-ratio figures above are my calculations from disclosed revenue and operating income; only the railway operating ratio percentages are directly disclosed.
